name: Wrath-Hollow
geological_features: Vast hollow interior detected by density measurements far below expected values
Surface riddled with deep sinkholes leading to internal voids
Unusual seismic echoes suggesting cathedral-scale interior spaces
specific_features: Interior voids contain atmosphere with different composition than the surface
Acoustic phenomena within the caverns that amplify to deafening volumes
description: Wrath-Hollow is a barren world whose most remarkable feature is not on its surface but beneath it. Density measurements reveal that the planet's interior is significantly hollow, riddled with void spaces of cathedral scale connected by tunnel networks that may span the entire mantle. Sinkholes dot the barren surface, offering access points to an interior world of darkness and echoes.

The thin surface atmosphere gives way, within the sinkholes, to a denser gaseous environment of different composition, warmer and richer in organic compounds than the surface air. Sound behaves strangely in the interior spaces, amplifying through resonance until even footsteps build to painful volumes that take minutes to decay.

Microbial life thrives on the interior cavity walls, sustained by chemical energy from reactions between the rock and the internal atmosphere. The organisms produce trace amounts of exotic matter as a metabolic byproduct, a discovery that has generated intense scientific and commercial interest despite the extreme difficulty of operating in the echo-plagued caverns.

The origin of the hollow interior is unexplained by standard planetary formation models. Some researchers theorize that a massive internal body was somehow extracted or consumed, leaving the shell behind. The acoustic amplification effect makes extended exploration psychologically grueling, as the planet seems to rage at every intrusion with exponentially amplified sound, a hollow world that screams when disturbed.
